abstract: We implement Grover's quantum search algorithmon a nuclear spin chain quantum computer, taking into Ising type interactions between nearest and second nearest neighbours into account. The performance of the realisation of the algorithm is studied by numerical simulations with four spins. We determine the temporal behaviour of the fidelity during the algorithm, and we compute the final fidelity as a function of the Rabi frequency. For the latter, we obtained pronounced maxima at frequencies which fulfil the condition of the 2πk-method with respect to the second nearest neighbour interactions.

specification.problem: Reconstruct a mathematical specification of Grover's search algorithm executed on a 4-spin nuclear-spin-chain (Ising) quantum computer with nearest- and second-nearest-neighbour couplings, driven by resonant radio-frequency (Rabi) pulses, including the fidelity figure of merit and the 2πk-method condition that the abstract reports as governing maxima of the final fidelity as a function of the Rabi frequency.
specification.reconstruction_scope: ONE smallest useful construction (chosen as an assumption since no experiment_scope was supplied): a 4-qubit (N=16) Grover search for a single marked basis state w (instance w=|1111>, the all-spins-flipped state), with (i) the ideal gate-level Grover iteration as the reference, (ii) a drift Ising Hamiltonian with nearest- and second-nearest-neighbour z-z couplings, (iii) selective rectangular RF pulses parameterised by a Rabi frequency Omega, (iv) the fidelity between the ideal and the pulse-driven state, and (v) the 2πk resonance condition for the Rabi frequency with respect to the second-neighbour coupling. Outside scope: the paper's specific pulse-sequence decomposition of oracle and diffusion operators into RF pulses and free evolutions, numerical coupling/Larmor values, the time-resolved fidelity curves and the numerically obtained positions of the fidelity maxima.

equations.label: Drift Ising Hamiltonian of the spin chain with nearest and second-nearest neighbour couplings
equations.description: Time-independent Hamiltonian of the four-spin chain in the static magnetic field: individual Zeeman terms plus Ising (z-z) couplings between nearest neighbours (J) and second-nearest neighbours (J').
equations.abstract_quote: taking into Ising type interactions between nearest and second nearest neighbours into account
equations.justification: The abstract specifies an Ising-type nuclear spin chain with nearest and second-nearest neighbour interactions; the explicit form, sign conventions and the factor 2 follow the standard Ising-spin-chain quantum-computer model and are not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Open chain of 4 spins with distinct Larmor frequencies omega_k so that spins are individually addressable
Sign/normalisation convention (-2J I^z I^z) is a choice; the paper may use a different convention
Only z-z (Ising) couplings, no flip-flop terms

equations.label: RF pulse Hamiltonian (rotating-wave approximation)
equations.latex: H_{\rm rf}(t) = -\Omega \sum_{k=1}^{4} \left[ I_k^{x}\cos(\nu t + \varphi) - I_k^{y}\sin(\nu t + \varphi) \right], \qquad H(t) = H_0 + H_{\rm rf}(t)
equations.description: Circularly polarised transverse RF field of Rabi frequency Omega, carrier frequency nu and phase varphi acting on all spins; a pulse tuned to nu = omega_k (shifted by the coupling-dependent offset of the desired neighbour configuration) rotates spin k selectively. Pulse duration tau with Omega tau = pi/2 or pi gives pi/2 or pi rotations on the resonant spin.
equations.justification: The abstract only names the Rabi frequency as the scanned parameter; the explicit form of the RF driving term is standard for RF-driven nuclear-spin quantum computers.
assumptions: Rectangular pulses of constant amplitude
Rotating-wave approximation valid (Omega, J, J' much smaller than omega_k)
Pulses are applied sequentially; free evolution under H_0 between pulses

equations.label: Ideal Grover iteration on 4 qubits
equations.latex: |s\rangle = \frac{1}{4}\sum_{x=0}^{15}|x\rangle,\quad O_w = \mathbb{1} - 2|w\rangle\langle w|,\quad D = 2|s\rangle\langle s| - \mathbb{1},\quad G = D\,O_w
equations.description: Gate-level reference algorithm: uniform superposition, phase oracle marking w, inversion about the mean, and the Grover iterate G. Basis state |x> = |x_1 x_2 x_3 x_4> with spin k encoding bit x_k (spin up = 0, spin down = 1), x = sum_k x_k 2^{4-k}.
equations.justification: Grover's algorithm is named in the abstract; its standard operator definitions are recalled as background, not extracted from the paper.
assumptions: Single marked item
Register ordering: spin 1 is the most significant bit

equations.label: Success amplitude and iteration count for N=16
equations.description: Exact success probability after r ideal Grover iterations for a single marked item in N=16; three iterations give sin^2(7 theta) ≈ 0.961.
equations.justification: Standard Grover analysis specialised to the abstract's four-spin case; the abstract does not state how many iterations were simulated.
assumptions: Single marked item
The paper may have simulated a different number of iterations (e.g. a single iteration)

equations.label: 2πk-method condition for the Rabi frequency with respect to the second-neighbour coupling
equations.description: A spin detuned by Delta from the carrier of a pi pulse (Omega tau = pi) performs a full 2πk rotation about its tilted effective field and returns to its initial state (up to phase) when the generalised Rabi angle is a multiple of 2π, suppressing the unwanted non-resonant transition. Taking the detuning produced by the second-nearest-neighbour coupling, |Delta| = 2J' (in the convention of eq_1), gives discrete Rabi frequencies Omega_k at which the fidelity is maximal; for a pi/2 pulse (tau = pi/(2 Omega)) the condition reads Omega = |Delta|/sqrt(16k^2-1).
equations.abstract_quote: we obtained pronounced maxima at frequencies which fulfil the condition of the 2πk-method with respect to the second nearest neighbour interactions
equations.justification: The abstract states that fidelity maxima occur at Rabi frequencies satisfying the 2πk condition with respect to J'. The generic 2πk formula is standard background for spin-chain quantum computers; identifying the relevant detuning with the second-neighbour splitting 2J' is an inference from the quote, and the exact numerical prefactor depends on the paper's Hamiltonian convention.
assumptions: Detuning magnitude |Delta| = 2J' follows the convention of eq_1; a different convention (e.g. J' I^z I^z without factor 2, or frequency units) changes the prefactor
Condition quoted for pi pulses; the paper may apply it to pi/2 pulses or both

equations.label: Fidelity of the realisation
equations.latex: F(t) = \left|\langle \psi_{\rm ideal}(t)|\psi(t)\rangle\right|^{2},\qquad |\psi(t)\rangle = \mathcal{T}\exp\!\left(-i\int_0^{t} H(t')\,dt'\right)|\psi(0)\rangle,\qquad F_{\rm final}(\Omega) = F(T_{\rm total})
equations.description: State fidelity between the pulse-driven state obtained by numerically integrating the Schrödinger equation under H(t) and the ideal gate-level state after the corresponding step of the algorithm; the final fidelity is evaluated at the end of the pulse sequence as a function of Omega.
equations.abstract_quote: We determine the temporal behaviour of the fidelity during the algorithm, and we compute the final fidelity as a function of the Rabi frequency
equations.justification: The abstract defines the figure of merit qualitatively (time-dependent and final fidelity vs Rabi frequency); the squared-overlap definition and the piecewise ideal reference are standard choices not confirmed by the abstract.
assumptions: Fidelity defined as squared overlap of pure states (the paper might use the overlap without squaring)
Ideal reference state is piecewise constant, equal to the ideal state after the most recently completed logical gate
hbar = 1

registers.name: spin chain
registers.role: Four nuclear spins I_1..I_4 forming the search register; spin k encodes bit x_k (spin up = 0, down = 1), spin 1 is the most significant bit

specification.initial_state: |\psi(0)\rangle = |0000\rangle (all spins aligned with the static field, idealised pure ground state); the uniform superposition |s> is then created by a selective pi/2 pulse on each spin.

steps.description: Initialise the chain in |0000> and apply a pi/2 RF pulse (Omega tau = pi/2) to each of the four spins in turn to prepare the uniform superposition |s> (Hadamard-like step).

Implement the oracle O_w for w = 1111 as a conditional phase flip using selective pulses on one spin conditioned (through the J, J' shifts) on the states of the other spins, interleaved with free evolution under H_0.
Implement the diffusion operator D = 2|s><s| - 1 as pi/2 pulses on all spins, a conditional phase flip on |0000> (same technique as the oracle), and pi/2 pulses again.
Repeat the oracle + diffusion block r times (instance r = 3 for N = 16).
Throughout, integrate the Schrödinger equation under H(t) and record F(t); at the end of the sequence record F_final(Omega), scanning Omega and comparing maxima with the 2πk values Omega_k.

specification.measurement: Projective measurement of all four spins in the z basis (computational basis); outcome x = 1111 is the search result with probability |<w|psi(T_total)>|^2 (ideal: sin^2(7 theta) for r = 3). In the numerical simulation no measurement is needed: the fidelity F is evaluated directly from the state vector.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Read the 4-bit outcome and verify it is the marked item; for the simulation, locate maxima of F_final(Omega) and compare with Omega_k = 2J'/sqrt(4k^2-1), k = 1,2,...
assumptions: No experiment_scope supplied: scope restricted to a single 4-qubit Grover search with one marked state w = 1111 and r = 3 iterations (choice of w and r is arbitrary)
Hamiltonian convention of eq_1 (factor 2J, 2J', hbar = 1) is assumed; the paper's convention is unknown
Only Ising (z-z) couplings, rotating-wave approximation, rectangular sequential pulses, no decoherence
The specific pulse-sequence decomposition of oracle and diffusion operators is a generic proposal, not the paper's sequence
Spin 1 is the most significant bit; spin up encodes 0
missing_information: Numerical values of Larmor frequencies omega_k, couplings J and J', pulse durations and total sequence time
The paper's exact pulse sequence realising the oracle and the diffusion operator, and the number of Grover iterations simulated
Precise definition of the fidelity (squared overlap or not) and of the ideal reference state during pulses
Whether the 2πk condition was applied to pi pulses, pi/2 pulses, or both, and the exact detuning used (prefactor relating Delta to J')
Numerical results: fidelity time traces and positions/heights of the fidelity maxima versus Rabi frequency
